title: Inter‑Service Communication
description: Learn how microservices talk to each other using REST, Feign clients, and messaging.

slides.title: Synchronous vs Asynchronous 📞📨
slides.content:
# Two Communication Styles

| Style | Example | Pros | Cons |
|-------|---------|------|------|
| **Synchronous** | HTTP/REST, gRPC | Simple, request‑response | Coupling, blocking, cascading failures |
| **Asynchronous** | Messaging (RabbitMQ, Kafka) | Loose coupling, resilient | Complexity, eventual consistency |

Both have their place. For many simple microservices, **REST over HTTP** is a great start.

quizData.question: Which communication style is synchronous?
quizData.explanation: HTTP/REST is synchronous because the client waits for a response. Messaging is asynchronous.

Resilience Patterns
slides.content: When microservices call each other, failures are inevitable. Use **circuit breakers** (like Resilience4j) to prevent cascading failures. Spring Cloud Circuit Breaker integrates with Resilience4j and Hystrix.
